sections.title: Bringing Unit 28 together
sections.content: The 1st-person plural imperative (-junk/-jünk) asked as a question turns into a suggestion: Menjünk moziba? -nék attaches to any verb's stem to say "I would..." (várnék, tanulnék), and the full conditional paradigm runs -nék/-nál/-na/-nánk/-nátok/-nának, harmonizing back or front. neked kellene aims general advice at one person; a bare -nál/-nél form (pihennél?) works as a gentler, more personal nudge. In a hypothetical ha sentence, BOTH clauses switch to the conditional: Ha lenne időm, elmennék moziba.

items.english: Shall we go to the cinema tonight?
If I had time, I'd go to the cinema.
It would be better if we left earlier.

sections.content: Both halves of a hypothetical ha sentence take the conditional in Hungarian, even though English often keeps only one half in "would" — ha lenne pairs with elmennék, never with elmegyek.
